pcs.pc_description: select the appropriate type of dredge for use in the plant
ensure the dredger unit is in complete floating condition and there is no grounding of the Unit at any point
check the dredger unit is appropriately positioned and anchored at all corners using winch ropes and spuds
transport the materials in the maintenance barge
assess the weight of the material and keep the load in the designated place with appropriate anchorage
check the slurry pump for the correct functioning
ensure the dredger pump is appropriately primed and the suction pipe is completely submerged inside water before starting the dredger pump

check and ensure all the operating parameters of the dredger unit, e.g. main motor temperature, mass flow meter reading, main motor ammeter reading, head feed bin level indicator reading, etc., are within the permissible limits
maintain the appropriate flow rate and pulp density of the dredger to match with the requirements for the operation of the up-gradation unit

maximize the dredge cutting depth to six meters below the surface of the water over the entire area by monitoring the depth indicator and by swinging mechanism to get the uniform pond bottom profile for the ease of plant shifting
maintain the required suction vacuum and discharge pressure of the dredger pump by using the pressure indicators provided on the unit
convey the slurry to the wet up-gradation unit maintaining parameters, such as feed rate, pulp density, head feed bin indicator, mass flow meter reading, etc

check the layout and condition of the components of the hydraulic system, such as the hydraulic power pack, accumulator, actuators, check valve, pressure control valve, flow control and direction control valves, hoses and their coupling
conduct operational checks on the areas of potential issues, e.g. unusual noises/ vibrations, blockages and obstruction, lubrication of drive head
ensure the surge bin level is within the safe operating range
flush the pumps with clean water following the standard procedure
follow the appropriate procedure for stopping the dredge pump, i.e. first stop the dredge pump and then hydraulic and other pumps
use the appropriate safety gear for anchor block shifting, winch wire rope handling, locking of winches, sandblasting, etc
maintain a safe distance from the pond edge in front of the dredge and avoid walking on the pontoons during the movement of dredge
follow the Safety Management Plan (SMP) and Emergency Management Plan (EMP) and encourage others to do the same
ensure the dredge deck floor is clean and tidy by washing away the spread oil, grease etc., using a water jet
follow the appropriate safety measures while working at haul roads, heights, dumps, sump area, stockyards, near moving parts, etc
ensure no unauthorized personnel is present on the maintenance barge during material handling
follow the standard signal while lifting materials
ensure coupling guards/ belt guards of pumps are in the correct position
ensure to switch off the lighting distribution board while cleaning the spiral with a water jet
use appropriate chain pulley, slings and ropes for loading and unloading materials
follow appropriate measures to avoid coming in contact with noxious fumes/ gases
maintain constant contact with the man standing outside through VHF wireless while dewatering inside the deck compartment
use headlamp of the recommended specification with proper gauge protection during deck cleaning
maintain the pontoon hand rails in good condition
use and follow caution and safety signs, stickers, and tags
